transcript: నాకు రెండు రోజులుగా ఛాతిలో నొప్పి ఉంది. శ్వాస తీసుకోవడం కష్టం.
translation: I have had pain in my chest for two days. It is difficult to breathe.

soap_note.subjective:
• Chief Complaint (CC): Severe chest pain for 2 days.
• History of Present Illness (HPI): Dull, pressure-like chest pain of constant nature, worsening significantly upon deep inspiration (pleuritic description). Associated with progressive dyspnea.
• Associated Symptoms: Patient denies radiation to left arm or jaw, nausea, vomiting, or diaphoresis.
soap_note.objective:
• Remote Vocal Consultation: Physical examination restricted by distance. Vocal contact only.
• Vocal Cues & Speech Attributes: Speech exhibits moderate distress and slight breathlessness between sentences.
• Recommended Vitals: Prompt evaluation of Blood Pressure, ECG, Heart Rate, and Oxygen Saturation (SpO2).
soap_note.assessment:
• Primary Suspected Diagnosis: Suspected Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS) vs. Pleuritic Chest Pain.
• Differential Diagnoses:
  1. Angina pectoris
  2. Pulmonary embolism
  3. Pericarditis / Costochondritis
• Clinical Rationale: Cardiopulmonary emergencies must be ruled out immediately due to the combination of chest pressure and shortness of breath.
soap_note.plan:
1. Immediate Interventions: Refer immediately to the nearest Emergency Department or Tertiary Hospital.
2. Patient Positioning: Advise patient to rest in a semi-Fowler's (upright) position.
3. Initial Therapy: Recommend Aspirin 325mg PO chewed immediately if no contraindications exist.
4. Red Flag Warnings: Seek emergency transport. Avoid all physical exertion.

triage.condition: Acute Chest Pain / Possible Coronary Syndrome

transcript: मुझे तीन दिनों से बहुत तेज बुखार है और बदन में दर्द है।
translation: I have had a very high fever for three days and body ache.

soap_note.subjective:
• Chief Complaint (CC): High-grade fever and generalized myalgia for 3 days.
• History of Present Illness (HPI): Acute onset of high-grade fever, accompanied by generalized body aches (myalgia), moderate headache, and severe fatigue. Fever is reported as continuous.
• Associated Symptoms: Denies dry cough, sore throat, vomiting, rash, or burning micturition.
soap_note.objective:
• Remote Vocal Consultation: Limited to voice analysis. No physical examination.
• Vocal Cues & Speech Attributes: Voice sounds weak and fatigued, but patient is coherent and oriented.
• Recommended Vitals: Measure core temperature, blood pressure, pulse, and check for skin rashes.
soap_note.assessment:
• Primary Suspected Diagnosis: Acute Febrile Illness of suspected viral etiology.
• Differential Diagnoses:
  1. Dengue Fever / Malaria
  2. Enteric Fever (Typhoid)
  3. Influenza / COVID-19
• Clinical Rationale: High-grade fever for 3 days with myalgia requires monitoring for local endemic vector-borne diseases.
soap_note.plan:
1. Immediate Interventions: Keep patient cool, rest, and start sponge baths if temperature exceeds 103°F.
2. Recommended Diagnostics: Advise Complete Blood Count (CBC) and malaria smear if fever persists for another 24 hours.
3. Symptomatic Treatment: Tab Paracetamol 650mg PO every 6 hours as needed for fever/pain. Maintain rich fluid intake (ORS, coconut water).
4. Red Flag Warnings: Seek urgent care if patient develops persistent vomiting, skin rashes, nosebleeds, or confusion.

triage.condition: Acute Febrile Illness / Possible Viral Syndrome

transcript: కడుపులో మంటగా ఉంది మరియు వాంతులు అవుతున్నాయి.
translation: There is a burning sensation in the stomach and vomiting is occurring.

soap_note.subjective:
• Chief Complaint (CC): Epigastric burning and vomiting for 24 hours.
• History of Present Illness (HPI): Severe burning sensation in the epigastric region (upper abdomen) for the past 24 hours, associated with three episodes of non-bilious, non-bloody vomiting. Worsened by ingestion of food.
• Associated Symptoms: Denies fever, diarrhea, melena, or radiating pain to the back.
soap_note.objective:
• Remote Vocal Consultation: Visual/abdominal palpation is not possible.
• Vocal Cues & Speech Attributes: Speech tone is stable; voice sounds slightly dry, suggesting mild dehydration.
• Recommended Vitals: Check blood pressure (orthostatic if possible), pulse rate, and assess oral mucosa hydration status.
soap_note.assessment:
• Primary Suspected Diagnosis: Acute Gastritis vs. Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD).
• Differential Diagnoses:
  1. Peptic Ulcer Disease (PUD)
  2. Early Viral Gastroenteritis
  3. Biliary Colic
• Clinical Rationale: Epigastric burning and recurrent vomiting suggest stomach lining irritation, with moderate risk of dehydration.
soap_note.plan:
1. Immediate Interventions: Avoid solid foods for the next 4-6 hours. Take small, frequent sips of ORS.
2. Recommended Diagnostics: If symptoms persist beyond 48 hours, consider stool evaluation or H. pylori testing.
3. Symptomatic Treatment: Proton Pump Inhibitor (e.g. Pantoprazole 40mg PO once daily before breakfast) and an antacid gel (e.g. Sucralfate) as directed.
4. Red Flag Warnings: Go to a clinic immediately if vomiting contains blood, stool becomes black/tarry, or abdominal pain becomes severe and localizes to the right lower quadrant.

transcript: எனக்கு இரண்டு முழங்கால்களிலும் கடுமையான வலி உள்ளது, நடக்க முடியவில்லை.
translation: I have severe pain in both of my knees and I am unable to walk.

soap_note.subjective:
• Chief Complaint (CC): Chronic bilateral knee pain, acutely worsened over the past week.
• History of Present Illness (HPI): Patient reports long-standing pain in both knees for several months. Pain has acutely worsened, rendering the patient unable to walk or bear weight comfortably. Morning stiffness is reported, lasting approximately 15 minutes.
• Associated Symptoms: Reports bilateral knee swelling; denies fever, chills, or pain in other joints.
soap_note.objective:
• Remote Vocal Consultation: Joint examination and range of motion tests cannot be physically performed.
• Vocal Cues & Speech Attributes: Slow, deliberate speech tone, consistent with chronic discomfort, but no acute respiratory distress.
• Recommended Vitals: Measure patient weight, blood pressure, and visually inspect for joint erythema or deformity.
soap_note.assessment:
• Primary Suspected Diagnosis: Bilateral Knee Osteoarthritis Flare-Up.
• Differential Diagnoses:
  1. Inflammatory Arthritis (e.g., Rheumatoid Arthritis)
  2. Gouty Arthropathy
  3. Anserine Bursitis
• Clinical Rationale: Slowly progressive bilateral joint pain with acute functional impairment (inability to walk) is highly suggestive of osteoarthritis flare-up.
soap_note.plan:
1. Immediate Interventions: Joint rest during the acute flare. Avoid deep squatting, kneeling, or sitting cross-legged.
2. Recommended Diagnostics: Plain X-ray of bilateral knees (standing AP and lateral views) and serum Uric Acid / Rheumatoid Factor checks.
3. Symptomatic Treatment: Tab Paracetamol 500mg PO every 8 hours as needed. Apply warm or cold compresses locally to the knees.
4. Red Flag Warnings: Seek medical review if a single joint becomes hot, highly erythematous, and accompanied by high fever (concerning for septic arthritis).

transcript: मुझे बहुत दिनों से खांसी है और सीने में जकड़न महसूस हो रही है।
translation: I have had a cough for many days and feel tightness in my chest.

soap_note.subjective:
• Chief Complaint (CC): Productive cough and chest tightness for over 10 days.
• History of Present Illness (HPI): Subacute onset of productive cough producing whitish sputum, associated with constant chest tightness and mild nasal congestion. Symptoms are worse at night.
• Associated Symptoms: Reports low-grade fever; denies shortness of breath at rest, hemoptysis, night sweats, or significant weight loss.
soap_note.objective:
• Remote Vocal Consultation: Auscultation is not possible.
• Vocal Cues & Speech Attributes: Occasional coughing audible during conversation. Respiration rate seems normal.
• Recommended Vitals: Measure body temperature, respiratory rate, and oxygen saturation (SpO2) at rest.
soap_note.assessment:
• Primary Suspected Diagnosis: Acute Bronchitis vs. Upper Respiratory Tract Infection (URTI).
• Differential Diagnoses:
  1. Atypical Pneumonia
  2. Cough-Variant Asthma
  3. Pulmonary Tuberculosis (given duration)
• Clinical Rationale: Cough lasting more than 10 days with chest tightness requires evaluation to rule out lower respiratory involvement or subacute infections like TB.
soap_note.plan:
1. Immediate Interventions: Stream inhalation twice daily. Remain hydrated with warm fluids.
2. Recommended Diagnostics: If cough exceeds 14 days, obtain a sputum smear for Acid-Fast Bacilli (AFB) and a chest X-ray.
3. Symptomatic Treatment: Oral expectorant syrup (e.g. Guaifenesin) and Paracetamol 500mg PO if fever rises. Avoid cold drinks.
4. Red Flag Warnings: Visit a physician immediately if breathing difficulty develops, sputum becomes bloody, or high-grade fever persists.
